subject: Appeal: orphaned prefetch token credits and VAT treatment
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@novametrics.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Finance Team <finance@novametrics.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected prefetch charges and VAT classification

Hi Kimberly —

We reviewed our November invoice and see a line item labeled ‘prefetch/kv-cache’ that generated ~1.2M embed token units. Our usage dashboard shows no corresponding spike on our side during the stated window (2026-11-15 02:00–07:00 UTC). We’ve attached the usage_export_202611.csv and the signed MOP for our account. Can you explain why this was billed and whether these tokens qualify for credits under the reserved-prefetch policy in our contract?

Also, the invoice applied VAT at 20% to the disputed line. We treat these as platform-side prefetch operations and expect the VAT handling to follow the EU reverse-charge language in section 4.3 of our agreement (even though our billing entity is US-based). Please confirm.

We’d appreciate a written breakdown (token-by-token if possible) and a temporary invoice hold while you investigate.

Thanks,
Alex Green
Head of Platform Reliability
Novametrics

Attachments: usage_export_202611.csv (csv, 120KB), signed-mop-2026-10.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

Subject: Re: Unexpected prefetch charges and VAT classification

Hi Alex — thanks for the note and the files. I’ve started a quick triage with billing ops; I’m copying Ben (metering lead) and Marissa (collections) so we can coordinate the evidence and credit pathway.

Next steps from us:
- Ben will pull the raw request logs and tokenization traces for the 2026-11-15 02:00–07:00 UTC window and map request IDs to your project IDs.
- Marissa will open a provisional invoice hold for the disputed line so collections won’t proceed while we investigate.
- I’ll review the MOP and the reserved-prefetch policy to see if the behavior qualifies for a credit.

Can you confirm whether Novametrics has any internal batch jobs that might have been re-run from a staging cluster recently? Any trace IDs or example request IDs in the CSV will speed us up.

I’ll follow up by EOD Wednesday with an interim status.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park

Subject: Re: Unexpected prefetch charges and VAT classification

Alex / Kimberly — quick update from metering: we traced the 1.2M embed units to an automated rekeying job that executed against a sandbox API key tied to Novametrics’ legacy staging project (project id nm-staging-3). The requests were proxied through an internal prefetch worker that erroneously flagged them as customer-originated prefetch (so they counted as billable).

Root cause summary: a tagging regression during the 2026-11-15 deployment caused the staging key to inherit production routing metadata. That made the prefetch worker apply a billable attribution.

Proposed remediation:
1) We’ll issue a full credit for the billed amount linked to those 1.2M tokens (provisional credit id: CR-20261202-NM).
2) We will reclassify the activity on your invoice as ‘internal staging prefetch — non-billable’ and remove VAT for that line.
3) Engineering will push a tagging fix and run a targeted re-run of internal tests; I’ll drop the change list here once merged.

I’ve attached the short log excerpt and request-id sample lines in the console export. Confirm with Finance whether the credit should be netted on December’s invoice or issued as a separate memo.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Metering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Unexpected prefetch charges and VAT classification

Alex — following Ben’s findings, finance is prepared to proceed with a provisional credit CR-20261202-NM for the full disputed amount. Two administrative items before we finalize:

1) VAT handling: since your billing entity is US-based but contract language references reverse-charge for EU VAT, can you confirm Novametrics’ EU tax registration number and the billing remit entity you want us to use for the credit memo? If you prefer the credit netted on the December invoice we will zero the line and reflect VAT reversal there; if you prefer a standalone credit memo we’ll mark it as VAT-exempt per our reclassification.

2) Evidence acceptance: we need a confirmation email from your security/ops team confirming the staging project id (nm-staging-3) is not production and that those runs were not customer-facing. A one-line confirmation is sufficient for our audit trail.

Once we have the EU VAT ID (if applicable) and the ops confirmation we’ll: apply the provisional credit, update the ledger, and issue either a credit memo or an invoice correction depending on your preference. Collections hold remains until resolved.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize the ledger fix this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
